RECORDS

Council. Bro. John D. Berg {H, '05) was appointed Temporary Presi

To facilitate the work of the Convention, the President assigned to the
Committee on Unfinished Business paragraphs III, V and VI of the Annual
Communication, relating to the Eleventh General Catalogue, New Song Book ,
and Printed Souvenirs.
There being no new business, at the request of the President, Vice-President
Bro. Parker-Smith took the chair.
The Committee to nominate an Executive Council presented the following
report :
The Committee appointed to nominate an Executive Council for the
coming year respectfully present the following resolutions for adoption by the
Convention assembled:
1. Resolved, that a hearty and sincere vote of thanks be extended to
the retiring Executive Council for their eminent and efficient services ren
dered the Fraternity during their term of office.
2. Resolved, that the present retiring Executive Coimcil, composed of
brothers following, be re-elected for the ensuing year:
Herbert L. Bridgman, Gamma '66.
George S. Coleman, Xi '76,
George H. Fox, Upsilon '67,
George W. Giddings, Lambda '92.
John V. Irwin, Delta '94.
The report was adopted.

Special Resolutions Xos. 1 and 2, introduced by Bro. Parker-Smith {H) ,
were carried.
The President appointed Bros. Parker-Smith and the Recorder a com
mittee to present to Dr. William H. Chandler the mvitation extended in Special
Resolution No. 1, and stated that he would personally deliver Special Resolu
tion No. 2 to Bro. Timothy L. Woodruff.*
A resolution offered by Bro. Pratt {Z) in relation to the initiation of Dr.
John H. Martindale, a son of the Founder, was referred to the Committee on
New Business.
On motion a recess was taken to 4:30 P. M.
The Convention re-assembled at 4:40 P. M., Bro. Bridgman in the chair.
The Committee on Credentials had no further report.
The Committee on the Annual Communication was still in session.
The Committee on Unfinished Business presented General Resolutions
Nos. 1, 2 and 3, concerning respectively the Catalogues on hand, the proposed
New Song Book and the Seventieth Anniversary Souvenirs. The resolutions
were duly adopted. No. 3 having been first amended by inserting the words
"pro rata" in the clause providing for distribution of the Souvenirs.
The Committee on New Business presented an amendment to the Consti
tution permitting the initiation of Dr. John H. Martindale. At the request of
Bro. Evans {H), the propriety of the amendment was explained by Bros.
Bradley {A), Chairman of the Committee, and Blanchard {E) . A letter on the
subject from Bro. Hugh W. Adams (.1), of Los Angeles, was read by Bro.
Coleman.
On roU-call the resolution was unanimously adopted {General Resolution .
Special Resolution No. 3, concerning the Phi Chapter, was duly carried.
The Committee appointed to invite Acting President Dr. William H.
Chandler to address the Convention reported that he was confined to his home
and would be unable to be present. A communication expressing the desire
of the Convention was left with the President's secretary.
Adjourned to Friday, May 12, 1905, 10 A. M.
*The resolution wat? telephoned from Bethlehem to Bro. Woodruff at his home in
Brooklyn, during a reception shortly after his own and his son's wedding.

FRIDAY, MAY 12, 1905
The Convention was called to order at 10:10 A. M., Bro. Bridgman m the
chair.
The minutes of yesterday's proceedings were read and approved.
A telegram from the Iota Chapter was read by the Recorder, stating that
delegates were
unavoidably detained, and that explanation by letter would
follow.
The Phi Chapter, through its delegates, submitted a communication and
information concerning a
proposed application for a charter from the Aztec
Club, of the University of Illinois. Referred to Committee on New Business.*
The Committee on the Annual Communication reported General Resolu
tions Nos. 5, 6 and 7 and Special Resolutions Nos. 4 and 5, which were
duly
adopted.
The Committee on New Business reported General Resolutions Nos. 8, 9
and 10 and Special Resolution No. 6.
As reported by the Committee, General Resolution No. 8 was as follows :
"
Resolved, That inasmuch as there is no provision in the Constitution
for the discipline of Retired Members, it be the sense of this Convention
that the delegates in Annual Convention assembled act on the expulsion of
a retired member. All data must be sent by the Chapter preferring charges
to the Executive Council four weeks before the Annual Convention."
Bro. Parker-Smith {H) suggested that a constitutional amendment might
be necessary, and moved to amend the resolution so that it would read as
follows :
"Resolved, that inasmuch as there is no provision in the Constitution
for the discipline of Retired Members, the question be referred to the Ex
ecutive Council and be reported for further action at the next Conven
tion."
The subject was discussed by Bros. Pratt (Z), Dickinson {'P'), Chapman
(W), Coleman (2) and Parker-Smith ^H).
On roll-call the amendment was carried by a vote of twenty-one to two, the
Zeta and Tau Chapters voting in the negative. The amended resolution was
then duly adopted {General Resolution No. 8).
General Resolutions Nos. 9 and 10 and Special Resolution No. 6 were
duly adopted.
*
Appendixes D, D' and D^.

8
A letter was read from Dr. William H. Chandler, Acting President of Lehigh
University, regretting that illness prevented his acceptance of the courteous
invitation to address the Convention. Dr. Chandler stated that he had many
intimate friends in the Psi Upsilon Fraternity, and was especially gratified
that Bethlehem, "the seat of one of the younger chapters," was selected for
our gathering this year, and considered that "Lehigh University is honored
thereby."
On motion of Bro. Bradley (/I), a fifteen minutes' recess was taken to
enable the Committee on New Business to draw up a supplementary report.
Recess, 11:20 to 11:35 A.M.
On re-assembly of the Convention the Committee on New Business re
ported General Resolution No. 11 and Special Resolutions Nos. 7 and 8,
which were didy adopted.
Bro. Ewing (BB) extended an invitation to the Convention to meet with
the Beta Beta Chapter in 1906.
Bro. Irwin, of the Executive Council, called attention to the office of
"Masters of the Rolls," provided for by the Convention of 1902, stating
that the offices had apparently not been filled by some of the Chapters, and
urging the importance of keeping the Chapter lists corrected to date.
There being no further business, the Convention adjourned sine die.
COURTLAND F. CARRIER, Jr., Eta '03,
Recorder.

(APPENDIX A)
THE COMMUNICATION OF THE EXECUTIVE COUNCIL TO THE
CONVENTION OF 1905
I. Membership. The active membership of the Fraternity on February
1, 1905, was 567, a decrease of 1 1 since 1904. A table of membership is hereto
appended.
II. In Memoriam. On Friday, July 15, 1904, Brother Edward Martindale,
Theta '36, our last surviving Founder, died at San Diego, California, in the
eighty-eighth year of his age. He was buried from St. Paul's Church, Los An
geles, on Sunday, July i7th. Twenty members of Psi Upsilon attended the
fimeral, representing the Pacific Psi Upsilon Union, the Psi Upsilon Associa
tion of Southern California, the Gamma and Epsilon Chapters, and, through
Brother Hugh W. Adams, Lambda '98, of Los Angeles, the Executive Council
of the Fraternity. We submit herewith a letter from Brother Adams in re
sponse to a telegraphic request for particulars, and an article from the Los
Angeles Times of July 18, 1904, containing a brief sketch of Brother Martindale's varied and honorable career.*
Special mention should be made of the death since the last Convention of
two other brothers conspicuous for lifelong devotion to the Fraternity, no less
than for high character and attainments�
Brother Joseph Roswell Hawley,
Psi '47, and Brother Willard Fiske, Psi '51, whose names have been for a gen
eration household words wherever Psi Upsilons gathered.
In the following list of deaths reported to the Council during the year
the Chapters particularly affected will recognize the loss of valued members:
Brothers William Henry Wilcox, '43, Delta; Adrian Van Sinderen, '64. Wil
liam Henry Hurlburt, '60, Frederic Wesson, '68, Henry Bruce McCarroll, '78,
Beta; Frank Henry Croker, '01, Sigma; Henry Hill Goodell, '62, Gamma;
Horace Harmon Burbank, '60, Kappa; Aaron Hale Burlingham, '48, Psi;
Justin Spaulding Barrows, '54, Nathan Gilbert Cheney and Samuel Robinson
Kelley, '69, Joseph Augustus Adlington and William Barnard Coleman, '73,
Eugene West Manning, '77, George Herrick Dains, '84, Xi ; Frederick .losiah
Nott, '74, Upsilon; Archer Brown, '72, Phi.
III. Eleventh General Catalogue. Pursuant to General Resoluti.on
No. 5, of the Convention of 1904, twenty-five copies of the catalogue of 1902
have been reserved by the Council and two hundred and thirty-four (234)
?Appendixes E and E'.

12
copies have been distributed to the Chapters. There yet remain in the hands
of the Council two himdred and seventy (270) copies of the catalogue which
were paid for by Chapter assessments, but which have not been called for by
the members entitled thereto. In order to save the expense of storage and
msurance and to furnish to those who may wish them the catalogues already
paid for, it would seem advisable that notice be sent to the indiNddual mem-'
bers, giving them an opportunity to secure the books upon payment of for
warding charges, or that the books be sent to the Chapters with a list of the
names of their members whose assessments have been credited therefor.
IV. Leaflet. On March 1, 1905, printed blanks were sent to the Chap
ters for the purpose of ascertaining the names, classes, residences and symbols
of all members initiated since February 1, 1902, not included in the last cata
logue. Reports have been received from all but two of the Chapters. As
soon as the remaining reports are received it is proposed to have all the lists
printed and proofs sent to the Chapters for revision and correction before
publication.
V. New Song Book. In response to requests for matter for the proposed
new edition of the Song Book, contributions have been received from six of the
Chapters. As nearly as we can now estimate, the cost of an edition of five
hundred copies would be eight hundred dollars. This includes a royalty of
forty cents a copy for each book sold, to be paid to Brother Karl P. Harring
ton, Editor of the Song Book of 1891. Brother Harrington gave his services
gratuitously for three years in the preparation of that book, and the Conven
tion of 1892 adopted a resolution {General Resolution No. 11) that out of the
proceeds of the sale of the second thousand copies of the Song Book the Ex
ecutive Council was authorized to pay him a royalty of forty cents per copy
sold. Eleven hundred and five copies were issued of the 1891 Edition, and no
royalties have been paid. As the new matter will constitute but a very small
portion of the new book, and as the plates of the last edition will be available
for the new, it seems proper to provide for the royalty approved by the Con
vention of 1892. Brother Harruigton is willing to undertake the necessary
work of supervising the preparation of the new book, if the Convention shall
so elect.
VI. Printed Souvenirs. About five hundred sets of the printed souven
irs of the Seventieth Anniversary Banquet, held at the Waldorf-Astoria on
November 24, 1903, are still undistributed. They include the menu card,
songs, and leaflet containing half-tones of all the Chapter Houses of the Fra
ternity. It was hoped that by the sale of the extra copies of the souvenirs

13
among members of the Fraternity not present at the banquet it might be
possible to pay the extra expenses of the occasion and add something to the
general fund of the Fraternity. The money for the leaflets was advanced per
sonally by Brothei' Irwin, of the Council, and there still remains a deficit of
1230.78, for which the Council is not officially or peraonaUy responsible to
Brother Irwiu. It would be gratifying, however, if the Convention would
authorize the payment to Brother Irwin, from the general fund, of the amount
advanced by him for which he has received no return. The souvenirs would,
in such event, be distributed pro rata among the Chapters, and if not desired
by the undergraduates would, we believe, be acceptable to many of the
alumni. The price of the souvenirs sold has been one dollar per set.
VII. Dr. John H. Martindale. Since the death of Brother Martindale
it has been represented to the Council by members of the Fraternity in Cali
fornia that Dr. John H. Martindale, his son, is thoroughly qualified by charac
ter and by long familiarity with the history and traditions of Psi Upsilon to
become a member of the Fraternity, and it has been asked whether it is pos
sible to accomplish this result. The only practicable method appears to be
that adopted in the case of Brother Leon Ferdinand Harvey, son of a Founder,
who was initiated by the Theta Chapter pursuant to a constitutional amend
ment. While the Fraternity is rightly conservative with respect to amending
its Constitution, it may be that the peculiar circumstances of the case would
justify this exception, which can never arise again. The Council, therefore,
submit the matter for your consideration.
VIII. The Phi Chapter. The Council sincerely regret to report to the
Convention the following facts concerning the Phi Chapter, which seem to
indicate a want of proper attention to the business of the Fraternity. Alone
among the Chapters the Phi has failed to comply with the provisions of General
Resolution No. 9, of the Convention of 1902, relating to Fraternity badges.
The explanation satisfactorily made in the fall of 1902 was that the Chapter
had given its order for badges to a local jeweler before it was aware that an
official jeweler had been selected, but no explanation has been offered since.
The Annual Report of the Chapter for 1905 was received on February 6th and
immediately returned for certain corrections. The corrected report was not
forwarded until April 17th. The printed blanks for the names of members
added to the rolls since February 1, 1902, were mailed to the Chapter on
March 1, 1905, but have not yet been returned.
IX. The Beta and Kappa. Pursuant to Special Resolution No. 6 of the
Convention of 1904, the Council wrote to the Beta and Kappa Chapters in-

14
quiring why the Chapters were not represented by delegates at that Conven
tion. Replies have been received from both Chapters. The Beta reports that
under the strict regulations of the authorities of Yale University leave of
absence would not be granted for the time required to attend a Convention so
far distant as Madison, Wisconsin. The Kappa reports that the expense inci
dent to the erection and furnishing of the new Chapter house rendered it fi
nancially impossible to defray the expenses of a delegate to the Convention.
Both the Beta and the Kappa express deep regrets at their inability to send
delegates to the Rho.
The Council would suggest that whenever it is impossible for any reason
for a Chapter to send an undergraduate delegate to the Annual Convention of
the Fraternity, a graduate of the Chapter living vrithin reasonable distance of
the place for holding the Convention should be delegated to represent the
Chapter.
X. Treasurer's Report. The report of the Treasurer is presented
herewith.
Respectfully submitted,
Herbert L. Bridgman
George S. Coleman
, George Henry Fox
George Welling Giddings
John V. Irwin
May 10, 1905.

ted States Army. Col. Martmdale was

ernor of Petersburg, Va., and held that

ent, at least, and his son, Dr. John H.
